risks: Low: farmers give time and allow observation; no procedures on animals beyond usual care. Risks are loss of trust if observation feels like inspection, and confidentiality of disease status.
consent: Written agreement from each farmer, covering the planning visit and unannounced observation visits, with the right to withdraw at any time.
data: Farm names are replaced by codes in the analysis file; disease information is not shared outside the practice.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus adapted to farms: small, tenant and family farms with little spare housing or labour, older farmers and farm workers with limited English may benefit less. Reach and adoption are reported by herd size and tenure, and priorities include low-cost measures.
effectiveness: Useful if observed adoption rises and the practice can see what delivery costs in vet time.
costs: About 50 vet half-days over six months; no equipment purchase by farmers.
grants: None; a positive result could support an application to a regional animal health fund.
partnerships: Practice vets, two farmer partners from the practice's client group, and the regional milk buyer's advisory team for dissemination.
rebPath: The practice will ask the veterinary school's human research ethics committee whether farmer participation needs review; no animal procedures are involved, so animal ethics approval is not required. ICH-GCP principles are followed for consent.
limitations: Few herds, one practice, no concurrent comparison, six-month follow-up only.
summary: Low-risk study with farmer consent, confidentiality of disease status and equity attention to small and tenant farms.
